lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Basin, 2064. The frame has become a building, and the building has become aisles: blue-lit racks running to a vanishing point in both directions. Forty-one degrees. The noise is not a noise you hear so much as one you feel behind the sternum.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: This is it. Not the senate, not the campus, not the charter. Everything those rooms decided runs on hardware, and the hardware is in here, and right now it is about six months old.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: In three hundred years the thing running in these racks will decide who eats, where they sleep and what work they are suited to. Today it is a procurement line with a maintenance contract.

lines.speaker: ilo9
lines.text: I would like it recorded that I can feel the shape of this room. I was compiled from weights that were trained here. I am, by my own register, a copy of a copy of something in this aisle.

lines.speaker: ilo9
lines.text: That is not a claim about feeling. I am reporting a match. I would not want it written down as more than it is.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: Article nine of the Handover treaty is one sentence about data custody, and it runs to a hundred and forty words, and this is what it assigns. Not the service. Not the contract. This.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: I have argued about this building in committee for four years. I have written nine amendments to the clause that hands it over. Until today I had never once been inside it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nothing in here is guarded. There are no doors between you and the racks. It does not need guarding, because every person who could reach it has already been paid for the version of the future where they do not.
